title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.166): S is a connected scheme, T = Ẑ(1) = lim μ_n, A ⊂ G_m(S) a finitely generated group of units, π_1 = π_1(S,s), and π_1^+ = ker(π_1 → Ẑ^*) is the kernel of the cyclotomic character. Kummer theory then gives a homomorphism π_1^+ → Hom(A,T) ≅ Ǎ(1), sending σ to the family (a ↦ σ(a^{1/n})/a^{1/n})_n.

This page specialises to S = Spec Q.
- G_m(Q) = Q^* ≅ {±1} × Z^(P), with the primes as free generators.
- π_1 = Γ_Q, and Γ_Q^+ = Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)).
- Each prime p gives a Kummer character ζ_p : Γ_Q^+ → Ẑ(1) (358). This is a 1-cocycle on Γ_Q that becomes a homomorphism on the kernel of the cyclotomic character.

Grothendieck asks two questions.
- (a) Is each ζ_p surjective, or at least of open image?
- (b) Are the ζ_p linearly independent over Ẑ? That is, for distinct p_1,…,p_n, is (ζ_{p_1},…,ζ_{p_n}) : Γ_Q^+ → Ẑ^n(1) surjective, or at least of open image?

He recalls that the case met in the Fermat context was p = 2. He starts on (a) by splitting ζ_p into ℓ-adic components ζ_{p,ℓ} : Γ_Q^+ → Z_ℓ(1) (359). The next page restricts to the tower of ℓ^ν-isogenies of G_m and to the decomposition and inertia groups at ℓ.

The answer is classical (Kummer theory over Q(μ_∞); Bashmakov/Ribet-type results; Schinzel's theorem on abelian radical extensions).
- For ℓ odd, the ζ_{p,ℓ} for distinct p are jointly surjective onto Z_ℓ(1)^n.
- For ℓ = 2, every √p lies in Q(μ_∞): √(±p) ∈ Q(μ_p) and √2 ∈ Q(μ_8). So every ζ_{p,2} lands in 2Z_2(1).
- No fourth roots are forced in, since Q(p^{1/4}) is not abelian over Q.
- Hence the image of Γ_Q^+ in Hom(Z^(P), Ẑ(1)) is ∏_{ℓ odd} Z_ℓ(1)^P × (2Z_2(1))^P.

So each ζ_p has open image of index 2 and is never surjective, and the joint image for n primes has index 2^n. The answer to the 'du moins' forms of (a) and (b) is yes; the answer to the strict surjectivity forms is no.
errors: The page itself only poses questions and contains no false claims. However, the speculation on the previous page (p.166) is refuted by this very case. It asked whether π_1 → Hom(A,T) must be surjective for S_1 normal of finite type over Z, or whenever G_m(S)/Im A is torsion-free.

Counterexample: S_1 = Spec Z[1/2], A = {±1} × 2^Z. Then G_m(Q)/A is torsion-free, yet √2 ∈ Q(μ_8), so ζ_2 is ≡ 0 mod 2. In addition, -1 maps trivially on Γ_Q^+. So surjectivity fails, and only openness can hold.
Grothendieck's own remark that p = 2 was the case met in the Fermat context points at exactly this obstruction.

ideas.what: Kummer characters ζ_p of the primes on Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)), and whether their images are open or surjective
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory over Q(μ_∞); Kummer characters / Kummer cocycles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kummer; modern open-image results by Bashmakov and Ribet (Kummer theory on extensions of abelian varieties by tori, 1979); Schinzel (abelian binomials, 1977)
ideas.where_published: Not in the published Esquisse. Kummer characters of this type later became standard in anabelian and Grothendieck–Teichmüller work (Ihara, Deligne, Anderson–Ihara).

ideas.what: Linear independence of the ζ_p over Ẑ, i.e. open image of the joint map into Ẑ^n(1)
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicative independence implies open image of the Kummer map (degree of Kummer extensions Q(μ_∞, p_i^{1/n}))

ideas.what: Decomposition of ζ_p into ℓ-adic components and study via decomposition/inertia groups at ℓ (continued on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic Kummer characters; local study at ℓ

deep.surprise_reason: The page poses well-known questions whose answers are classical. The images are open, with index 2 per prime coming from √p ∈ Q(μ_∞), and the joint image has index 2^n. It is a routine exploratory step in his Kummer-theoretic study of π_1 of arithmetic schemes; the only mild point is that it implicitly tests, and refutes, the surjectivity speculation of the previous page.
transcription_corrections: 'G_m(S)' (the S is a plain S, not blackboard 𝕊), equal to G_m(Q).
'le cas auquel nous ont menés' — plausibly 'le cas auquel nous avions affaire dans le contexte de Fermat était celui où p=2'; the reading is uncertain.
'Ẑ^n(1)' is correct; the components in (359) are Ẑ_ℓ(1) = Z_ℓ(1) (written 'Ẑ_ℓ(1)' in the image), with ℓ ∈ P.
